title: Travel and Transport
description: Learn how to talk about different types of transport, buy tickets, ask for directions, and describe travel experiences in English. Perfect for A1 completers who travel or plan to travel abroad.

content.content: {"time":1700000101000,"blocks":[{"id":"aB1cD2eF3g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"There are many ways to travel on land. Here is important vocabulary:"}},{"id":"hI4jK5lM6n","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["bus — a large vehicle that carries many passengers on a fixed route","train — travels on rails between cities or towns","tram — like a bus but runs on rails in the city","underground / metro / subway — a train that runs under the ground in a city","taxi / cab — a car you pay to take you somewhere","car — a private vehicle"]}},{"id":"oP7qR8sT9u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"We say: go by + transport → I go to work by bus. She travels by train."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

phrases.text: I go to work by bus.
phrases.translation: Я езжу на работу на автобусе.

content.text: I go to work by bus. She travels by train. They take the underground.

content.content:
{"time":1700000102000,"blocks":[{"id":"vW0xY1zA2b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Not all transport has a motor! Some common ways to get around:"}},{"id":"cD3eF4gH5i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["bicycle / bike — you pedal it yourself","motorbike / motorcycle — like a bike but with a motor","scooter — a small motorbike or electric scooter","on foot / walk — no vehicle, just your legs!"]}},{"id":"jK6lM7nO8p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Note the prepositions: by bike, by motorbike, on foot (not 'by foot')."}},{"id":"qR9sT0uV1w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past simple examples:
Yesterday I cycled to school. / We walked to the park. / She rode her motorbike to work."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I usually go by bike. Yesterday it was raining, so I went on foot.

content.text: I usually go to school [by] bike. Yesterday it was raining, so I went [on] foot. My brother rides a [motorbike] to work every day.

content.content: {"time":1700000103000,"blocks":[{"id":"xY2zA3bC4d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"For long-distance or international travel, we often use air or water transport:"}},{"id":"eF5gH6iJ7k","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["plane / aeroplane / airplane — flies through the air","helicopter — a small aircraft with spinning blades","ship — a large boat that crosses seas and oceans","ferry — a boat that carries people and cars across a river or short stretch of sea","cruise ship — a very large ship for holiday travel"]}},{"id":"lM8nO9pQ0r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful phrases: I flew to London. / We took the ferry to France. / They travelled by ship."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I flew to London. We took the ferry to France. They travelled by ship.

topics.title: Module 2: At the Station or Airport

content.content:
{"time":1700000104000,"blocks":[{"id":"sT1uV2wX3y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When you travel by train, you need to know this vocabulary:"}},{"id":"zA4bC5dE6f","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["ticket — the document that allows you to travel","single ticket — for one journey, one direction","return ticket — for a journey there and back","platform — where you wait for and board the train","departure — when the train leaves","arrival — when the train arrives","delay — when the train is late"]}},{"id":"gH7iJ8kL9m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key phrases:
I'd like a return ticket to London, please.
Which platform does the train leave from?
Is the train on time?"}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content:
{"time":1700000105000,"blocks":[{"id":"nO0pQ1rS2t","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Read this typical dialogue at a train station ticket office:"}},{"id":"uV3wX4yZ5a","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Clerk: Good morning. How can I help you?
Passenger: I'd like a return ticket to Edinburgh, please.
Clerk: When would you like to travel?
Passenger: Tomorrow morning. The first train, please.
Clerk: That's the 7:45. Standard class or first class?
Passenger: Standard class, please. How much is that?
Clerk: That's £62. Would you like a window seat?
Passenger: Yes, please. Thank you!"}},{"id":"bC6dE7fG8h","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key phrases from the dialogue:
- I'd like... (= I would like — polite request)
- How much is that?
- Standard class / first class
- Window seat / aisle seat"}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.targetPhrase: I'd like a return ticket to Edinburgh, please. Standard class.

content.text: I'd like a return ticket, please. Standard class. How much is that?
I'd [like] a return ticket to Paris, please. [How] much is that? Do you have a [window] seat available? The train [departs] at half past eight.

content.content: {"time":1700000106000,"blocks":[{"id":"iJ9kL0mN1o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Airports can be confusing! Learn this essential vocabulary:"}},{"id":"pQ2rS3tU4v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["check-in — the process of registering for your flight and dropping off luggage","boarding pass — the document you need to get on the plane","gate — the area where you wait before boarding the plane","passport control — where officials check your passport","customs — where officials check what you are bringing into the country","luggage / baggage — your bags and suitcases","hand luggage — small bag you carry onto the plane","flight — a journey by plane"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content:
{"time":1700000107000,"blocks":[{"id":"wX5yZ6aB7c","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When you are lost, you need to ask for directions. Here are useful phrases:"}},{"id":"dE8fG9hI0j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Asking:
Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
Where is the nearest bus stop?
Is it far from here?"}},{"id":"kL1mN2oP3q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Giving directions:"}},{"id":"rS4tU5vW6x","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Turn left / right — at the corner, turn in that direction","Go straight ahead / straight on — keep going in the same direction","Take the first / second turning on the left/right","It's on the left / right","It's opposite / next to / near + place","Cross the road / bridge — go to the other side"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.targetPhrase: Go straight ahead and turn left at the traffic lights.

content.text: [Excuse] me, how do I get to the museum? Go [straight] ahead and [turn] left at the traffic lights. The museum is [next] to the park. It's about ten minutes on [foot].

mistakeItems.text: Go straight forward until the lights.
mistakeItems.correctText: Go straight ahead until the lights.

pairs.english: Excuse me, where is the nearest metro station?
Turn right at the traffic lights.

content.text: Excuse me! Turn left at the traffic lights. It is opposite the bank.

options: keep going in the same direction

questions.text: You ask: 'Is it far?' The person says: 'It's about a 5-minute walk.' This means ___.
options: you need to take a bus

content.content: {"time":1700000108000,"blocks":[{"id":"yZ7aB8cD9e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"These are essential phrases for any traveller:"}},{"id":"fG0hI1jK2l","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Arriving at the hotel: I have a reservation. / I'd like to check in.","Asking about transport: Does this bus go to the city centre?","Problems with luggage: My suitcase is missing. / I lost my bag.","Getting on transport: Is this seat taken?","Paying: How much is a ticket to...?"]}},{"id":"mN3oP4qR5s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past simple forms to know: go → went, take → took, fly → flew, drive → drove, lose → lost"}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content: {"time":1700000109000,"blocks":[{"id":"tU6vW7xY8z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"When you talk about a past journey, use the past simple tense. Key vocabulary for describing a trip:"}},{"id":"aB9cD0eF1g","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["journey — the act of travelling from one place to another","trip — a short journey, often for a purpose","destination — the place you are travelling to","sightseeing — visiting famous and interesting places","souvenir — a small gift you buy to remember a place","accommodation — the place where you stay (hotel, hostel, etc.)"]}},{"id":"hI2jK3lM4n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful time expressions: last summer, three days ago, in March, last year."}},{"id":"oP5qR6sT7u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Example: Last summer I went to Spain. I flew from London. I stayed in a small hotel near the beach. I went sightseeing and bought souvenirs."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Last summer I went to Spain. I stayed in a hotel near the beach and went sightseeing every day.
Last year I went on a [trip] to Italy. My [destination] was Rome. I [stayed] in a small hotel in the city centre. I spent two days [sightseeing]. I [bought] many souvenirs for my family.

content.content: {"time":1700000110000,"blocks":[{"id":"vW8xY9zA0b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Travel doesn't always go smoothly! Here is vocabulary for common travel problems:"}},{"id":"cD1eF2gH3i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["delayed — the transport is late","cancelled — the journey does not happen at all","missed the train/bus/flight — you arrived too late and it left without you","lost luggage — your bags did not arrive at the destination","overbooked — too many tickets were sold (common on flights)","traffic jam — cars are not moving on the road"]}},{"id":"jK4lM5nO6p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Phrases to use: My flight was cancelled. / I missed my bus. / My luggage was lost. / There was a terrible traffic jam."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}
